title: U.S. House · Arizona's 4th District
area: South-central Phoenix metro area, including Tempe, Ahwatukee, part of Chandler, and part of south Phoenix.

context.text: Incumbent Democrat Greg Stanton, first elected to this seat in 2022 (he previously represented the old AZ-9), defeated Kai Newkirk 68.1%-31.9% in the July 21, 2026 Democratic primary, the only contested primary involving a sitting Arizona U.S. House incumbent in 2026. Zuhdi Jasser won the Republican primary unopposed. Tisha Benoit won the No Labels Party primary over John Fillmore. Steven Sanders is running as a No Labels Party write-in candidate in the general election. Cook Political Report rated the district D+4; in 2024 Stanton defeated Kelly Cooper 52.7%-45.5%.

candidates.name: Greg Stanton
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative, AZ-4 (since 2019, this seat since 2023)
candidates.ballotNote: Won the July 21, 2026 Democratic primary, 68.1%-31.9%, over Kai Newkirk

summary.text: Greg Stanton is the Democratic incumbent for Arizona's 4th Congressional District and an attorney by training. He served on the Phoenix City Council, as Arizona deputy attorney general, and as mayor of Phoenix from 2012 to 2018 before being elected to the U.S. House in 2018. He serves on the Transportation and Infrastructure and Foreign Affairs committees and the Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, and is seeking another term.

background.text: Born in Long Island, New York, in 1970; graduated from Cortez High School in Arizona.

Earned a B.A. in political science and history from Marquette University in 1992 and a J.D. from the University of Michigan in 1995. His official biography says he graduated from Marquette on a Harry S. Truman Scholarship.
Worked as an attorney before and between public offices.
Served on the Phoenix City Council from 2000 to 2009 (his official biography describes nine years on the council).
Served as deputy attorney general of Arizona from 2009 to 2010.

Served as mayor of Phoenix from 2012 to 2018. His official biography says he focused on innovation and trade, bioscience and higher education investments, and a voter-approved public transportation plan that funded light rail expansion, faster bus service and road modernization.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2018, representing Arizona's 9th District until redistricting placed him in the 4th District for the 2022 election.

Committee assignments for 2025-2026: Transportation and Infrastructure (subcommittees on Aviation; Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management; and Highways and Transit), Foreign Affairs, and the Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party. He earlier served on the Judiciary Committee (2019-2022).

According to his official biography, he co-founded a congressional caucus on heat-related policy, was named the Most Effective Democrat on Transportation Policy by the Center for Effective Lawmaking in 2025, and was named 2025 Elected Leader of the Year by the AZ AFL-CIO.
His official biography states that he is a husband and father of two children living in Arizona.

positions.summary: Says he supports restoring a woman's right to reproductive care and protecting access to contraceptives and IVF.
positions.quote: That includes restoring a woman’s right to safe, comprehensive reproductive care and protecting access to contraceptives and IVF.

positions.summary: Introduced the Fund Schools, Not ICE Act with Reps. Ansari and Grijalva, which would transfer unobligated ICE funding from the 2025 reconciliation law to Title I school grants and require DHS to sell 11 recently purchased warehouse detention facilities.

Led a House resolution to terminate the national emergency used to impose tariffs on Canada, and has backed the Prevent Tariff Abuse Act, which would bar tariffs under a national emergency without congressional approval.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (Aviation Subcommittee; Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management Subcommittee; Highways and Transit Subcommittee), the House Committee on Foreign Affairs, and the Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.name: Zuhdi Jasser
candidates.ballotNote: Won the July 21, 2026 Republican primary unopposed
candidates.currentRole: Physician; retired U.S. Navy lieutenant commander

summary.text: Zuhdi Jasser is a physician and U.S. Navy veteran (Lieutenant Commander), and the Republican nominee for Arizona's 4th Congressional District. He founded the American Islamic Forum for Democracy and is also affiliated with the Muslim Reform Movement.

background.text: Born November 17, 1967, in Canton, Ohio, to parents who immigrated from Syria; raised in Appleton and then Neenah, Wisconsin.

Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee and a medical degree from the Medical College of Wisconsin in 1992; according to his campaign website, both were part of an accelerated program funded by a U.S. Navy scholarship.

Served in the U.S. Navy as a medical officer, retiring as a lieutenant commander; his campaign website says he was honorably discharged in 1999 after 11 years of service. His tours included the USS El Paso and the Office of the Attending Physician to Congress. (Ballotpedia lists service from 1988 to 1999; an earlier entry giving 1993 was corrected.)
Moved to Phoenix after leaving the Navy, joined his father's medical practice and later founded the Jasser Center for Comprehensive Care; says he has practiced primary care for over two decades.
Founded the American Islamic Forum for Democracy in 2003 and co-founded the Muslim Reform Movement; has testified before Congress on political Islam.
Appointed in March 2012 by Senate Minority Leader Mitch McConnell to a two-year term on the U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom.
Has been affiliated with the Arizona Medical Association, the Maricopa County Board of Health, the Area Agency on Aging and NotMyKid.
According to his campaign website, he lives in Phoenix with his wife, Gada, and their three children.

priorities.text: His campaign site's sections cover balancing the budget, strong borders, education, health care and national security, including rebuilding military readiness.
Says he will work on costs, spending and patient-centered health care.
priorities.quote: I will fight to lower costs, rein in spending, and make healthcare more affordable and patient-centered.

priorities.text: Lists transparency, accountability and an end to congressional stock trading.
priorities.quote: I will fight for greater transparency and accountability, an end to congressional stock trading, fiscal responsibility, and an independent voice for AZ-04.
I support a Balanced Budget Amendment to the United States Constitution.

positions.summary: Supports 'educational freedom' and policies that direct public funding to students rather than school systems, including empowering parents' school choices.
positions.quote: I support educational freedom in education, and funding students — not systems.

statements.quote: protecting the American Dream also means protecting our borders.
We need to stop subsidizing our ailments and start solving them.

candidates.researchNotes: Reviewed his campaign site and 2026 Ballotpedia survey. Added statements on immigration and health care, which state priorities but not a side on the guide's exact statements, plus three priorities. His school-choice position was already recorded. Nothing found on abortion, guns, taxes, climate or tariffs.

candidates.name: Tisha Benoit
candidates.ballotNote: Won the July 21, 2026 No Labels Party primary, 65.4%-34.6%, over John Fillmore

summary.text: Tisha Benoit is the No Labels Party nominee for Arizona's 4th Congressional District. She is a healthcare practitioner and small business owner who describes herself as an Arizona native who grew up in the district. Her campaign themes, per her Ballotpedia survey, are healthcare affordability and access, Arizona water security, and economic opportunity and government accountability.

background.text: According to her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, she is an Arizona native who grew up in District 4 and graduated from Marcos de Niza High School.
Describes earning a bachelor's degree in Health Science, a master's degree in Traditional Chinese Medicine, and a doctorate in Acupuncture and Chinese Medicine.
Says she has been a small business owner in Arizona with a healthcare practice focused on women's health.
Says her community service includes volunteering on a medical mission in India and helping raise funds to build water wells in Cambodia.

priorities.text: Lists health care affordability and access as a key message.
priorities.quote: Healthcare Affordability & Access — Lower costs, expand access, strengthen prevention, and give patients more transparency and choice.

priorities.text: Lists water security as a key message.
priorities.quote: Arizona Water Security — Protect Arizona’s long-term water supply through responsible management, conservation, and practical innovation.

priorities.text: Says balancing the federal budget would be the central issue of her campaign.
priorities.quote: I am running for Congress to make balancing the federal budget the central issue of this campaign.

positions.summary: On her campaign website she says she supports school choice and that public schools must also be strong.
positions.quote: I support school choice, but I also believe public schools must be strong because the majority of our children will continue to attend them.

statements.quote: I don't support throwing out everything we have and starting over with a massive government-controlled system.
statements.context: On her campaign website's issues page

statements.quote: Build more. Remove unnecessary barriers. Protect Arizona resources. Help people move toward ownership rather than permanent dependency.
statements.context: On her campaign website's issues page

statements.quote: People who commit violent crimes or pose national-security threats should be removed.
statements.context: On her campaign website's issues page

statements.quote: I believe in science, innovation and environmental responsibility. But I don't believe working families should be punished with dramatically higher energy bills in the name of environmental policy.
statements.context: On her campaign website's issues page

statements.quote: And Congress must reclaim its constitutional responsibility over war.
statements.context: On her campaign website's issues page

statements.quote: Regarding conflicts such as Ukraine and the Middle East, I believe Congress has a responsibility to ask hard questions before committing American money or weapons
statements.context: On her campaign website's issues page

candidates.researchNotes: Reviewed her campaign home page and issues page (written as debate talking points), plus her 2026 Ballotpedia survey. Added one position (school choice) and six statements quoted as written. No statement found on abortion, guns, taxes on high earners, minimum wage or tariffs; her home page says spending cuts and additional revenue would both be 'on the table' without naming who would pay.

candidates.name: Steven Sanders
candidates.ballotNote: Running as a No Labels Party write-in candidate in the general election

summary.text: Steven Sanders is a No Labels Party write-in candidate for Arizona's 4th Congressional District. A Phoenix native and U.S. Army veteran, he has worked as an aviation mechanic and manager. He also ran as a write-in candidate for U.S. Senate in Arizona in 2024.

background.text: Born in Phoenix, Arizona; graduated from Sunnysloe High School (as spelled by Ballotpedia) and attended Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University.
Served in the U.S. Army from 1986 to 1991.
Career experience includes work as a manager and as an aviation mechanic with an FAA airframe and powerplant license.
Ran as a write-in candidate for U.S. Senate in Arizona in 2024, receiving 92 votes (0.0 percent), listed as an Independent.
Has been affiliated with the Roosevelts Rough Rider (as listed by Ballotpedia) and the Boy Scouts of America.

priorities.text: Lists economic growth and domestic manufacturing as an area of passion (2024 survey).
priorities.quote: Building the economy and brining manufacturing back to the U.S.

priorities.text: Says reducing government debt is part of the legacy he wants (2024 survey).
priorities.quote: If I can save future generation from crushing government debt that would be a good thing.

positions.summary: In his 2024 Ballotpedia survey (as a U.S. Senate candidate), he said people in the country illegally should be returned and the border closed to free travel.
positions.quote: Immigration needs to be addressed and the illegals that are here need to be returned back home and the border needs to be closed from free travel into this country.

statements.quote: Abortion is no longer a federal matter since the Supreme court said it violates the states rights to decide what the people want.
statements.context: In his 2024 Ballotpedia survey, completed as a 2024 U.S. Senate candidate

statements.quote: We need to stop all department mandates and allow the production of oil and gas to resume in this country to make us self reliant and prosperous.
statements.context: In his 2024 Ballotpedia survey, completed as a 2024 U.S. Senate candidate

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website or 2026 statements found. Everything here is from his 2024 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, completed when he ran for U.S. Senate; his views may have changed. He is a No Labels Party write-in candidate.

researchNotes: Greg Stanton's specific 2026 issue positions were not found beyond committee assignments and biography; his campaign website's issues pages did not render usable content in this environment. No campaign website or detailed public statements were found for Tisha Benoit (No Labels Party) or write-in candidate Steven Sanders within this research session's time budget; both entries are marked minimal. Per the division-of-labor guidance, Stanton's federal floor votes and FEC finance totals are added separately by script. Biography gaps: no campaign website or news profile was found for Tisha Benoit or Steven Sanders, so their biographies rest on Ballotpedia (Benoit's is her own survey answers); Stanton's official biography does not give his birthplace or birth year, which come from Ballotpedia.
